      <title>Manchester United 0-3 Bournemouth, Liverpool 2-0 Brighton and more: clockwatch – as it happened</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/oct/25/manchester-united-v-bournemouth-liverpool-v-brighton-and-more-premier-league-live</link>
      <description><p>Bournemouth humiliated Manchester United to leave Michael Carrick on the brink, while Liverpool beat Brighton, Newcastle won at Palace and Hull drew with Brentford </p><p><strong>Otherwise, Carrick goes for ballast in the midfield, with Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, which makes sense, but in front of him, there’s a palpable lack of magic.</strong> Matheus Cunha, hooked at half-time in Como, drops out, with Amad one of the least dreadful when he came on, coming in on the right. His numbers tell us he’s not the standard required, but he offers good out-of-possession work and gives the team balance, such as it is, the only dribbles in a team severely lacking one v one ability.</p><p>Otherwise, Mason Mount, every manager’s favourite, is relocated to the left, while Bryan Mbeumo continues up front in the absence of Benjamin Sesko – which tells us plenty about what Carrick thinks of Joshua Zirkzee, despite his goal in midweek.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/oct/25/manchester-united-v-bournemouth-liverpool-v-brighton-and-more-premier-league-live">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Osula and Barnes’ second-half burst sees Newcastle pile pressure on lacklustre Palace</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/crystal-palace-newcastle-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>The first half was one of the worst 45 minutes of football in Premier League history. The pass completion rate was a meagre 72.8%, although it felt lower. There were only two shots on target. The sun kept popping out from behind the clouds to take a look, and then going back in again, appalled. And the really bad news for Crystal Palace is that, for them, that was the good bit.</p><p>Newcastle were much improved after the break. Will Osula touched in a Jacob Murphy cross two minutes after half-time, Joe Willock had an effort ruled out for a marginal offside five minutes later, and Harvey Barnes completed a slick passing move six minutes after that. A smattering of boos from the home fans made clear what everybody already knew. Quarter of an hour of proper football had been enough to win the game, and that leaves Pierre Sage under significant pressure.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/crystal-palace-newcastle-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Michael Carrick on the brink after Manchester United are humiliated by Bournemouth</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/manchester-united-bournemouth-premier-league-match-report-michael-carrick</link>
      <description><p>After Bruno Fernandes was dropped for “pure football” reasons – according to Michael Carrick – could Manchester United actually win a game of football?</p><p>The answer, again, was a resounding, humiliating no, and if the manager’s job remains in real peril, you have to wonder, too, if this beleaguered team should steel themselves for a relegation dogfight. They lack imagination, cohesion, fight, confidence and anything resembling joy, and so, now they hover a point above the drop zone, survival cannot be taken for granted.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/manchester-united-bournemouth-premier-league-match-report-michael-carrick">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/liverpool-brighton-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Brighton’s emphatic run was blown off course at Anfield as Liverpool moved up to fourth with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It is Liverpool, convincing winners on home soil for the first time this season in the Premier League, who looked upwardly mobile.</p><p>Florian Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Alexander Isak converted his sixth league goal of the campaign to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive Premier League wins. Brighton’s winning streak had included 15 goals and none against but there was neither attacking verve nor defensive resilience on show from Fabian Hürzeler’s side. Liverpool had a monopoly on both, and the sight of Bradley Barcola racing back to defend and Ronald Araújo thundering into challenges will have satisified Iraola just as much as the incisiveness up front.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/25/liverpool-brighton-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Mathys Tel scored a fine solo goal to set the seal on a rare Spurs victory at the Bridge</p><p><strong>The teams take to the pitch.</strong> Chelsea in blue, Spurs in white, and it won’t be long before every shirt is soaking wet. Has the signature work of the Harry J All Stars ever been so apposite? We’ll be off in a couple of minutes.</p><p><strong>Roberto De Zerbi also speaks to Sky.</strong> “James Maddison is a very important player … he brings personality, qualities, experience … a different position on the pitch … he’s a different player to Conor Gallagher or [Omar] Marmoush as a number ten … we have to find him in the right moment in the best position … [Dominic Solanke] felt fatigue after Coventry … I am lucky to have a big squad with many different solutions … so I took the decision [to rest him] but the game is 90 minutes.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/oct/24/chelsea-v-tottenham-premier-league-live">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/ipswich-nottingham-forest-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer.</p><p>Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/ipswich-nottingham-forest-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/crystal-palace-and-newcastle-face-off-with-both-in-search-of-season-kickstart</link>
      <description><p>Pierre Sage and Matthias Jaissle face some key questions: both were appointed this summer yet form, and results, have proved elusive</p><p>Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/27/crystal-palace-rayo-vallecano-conference-league-final-match-report">became used to success under Glasner</a> and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. <strong>EA</strong></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/23/crystal-palace-and-newcastle-face-off-with-both-in-search-of-season-kickstart">Continue reading...</a></description>
